title: Refactor intent dispatch to use Set instead of long || chains
problem: Webhook route.ts line 1579: if (intent === 'balance' || intent === 'recent' || intent === 'summary' || ... 11 conditions). This is hard to read and error-prone when adding new intents. Should use const ROUTED_INTENTS = new Set(['balance', 'recent', ...]) and check with ROUTED_INTENTS.has(intent).
solution: Already refactored: webhook/route.ts now uses ROUTED_INTENTS Set with .has() instead of 11-condition || chain. Line 1617: if (ROUTED_INTENTS.has(intent)).
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-22

title: Add integration tests for intent pipeline
problem: Intent changes (detectIntent, executeIntentQuery, handleIntent) have zero test coverage. Changes are deployed with only type-checking. A bad regex or broken query case would only be caught in production. Need at minimum tests for balance, summary, and search intents with real Prisma queries.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-22 | WONTFIX: Intent pipeline deleted in LIFF→webapp pivot (commit 89b6e17). No pipeline to test.

title: FinanceContext.tsx exceeds 800-line limit
problem: FinanceContext.tsx is 1073 lines (273 over the 800-line rule). Contains account CRUD, transaction CRUD, category/tag CRUD, budget CRUD, soft delete/trash, and state management all in one file. Should extract trash logic and budget logic into separate context slices or hooks.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-27

title: handleAccountFormStep has no unit tests
problem: The handleAccountFormStep function (~80 lines) in src/lib/intent-router.ts has branching logic across 4 form steps, type detection, number parsing, and confirmation matching — but zero tests. Needs unit tests with mocked session-memory and prisma to verify each step transition and edge cases (invalid balance, unexpected input during confirm, etc).
solution: Added 20 unit tests covering all form steps: cancel (3 tests), name (1), type (5), balance (6), confirm (5). Uses mocked session-memory and prisma. Tests verify step transitions, type detection (number + text), amount parsing, account creation, reconciliation, edit reset, and cancel from any step.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-27

title: No cancel button during account creation form
problem: Account creation form (4-step multi-turn via LINE chat) has no way for users to cancel mid-flow. If someone types 'เพิ่มบัญชี' by accident, they're stuck in the form for 5 minutes (TTL) or must complete all 3 steps to reach the confirm step where cancel is available. Should add a 'ยกเลิก' quick reply button during form steps.
solution: Added cancel detection at top of handleAccountFormStep - checks for 'ยกเลิก' or 'cancel' at any step (name/type/balance/confirm). Added 'พิมพ์ "ยกเลิก" เพื่อยกเลิก' hint to name, type, and balance error prompts. Confirm step already had cancel option.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-27

title: Middleware has hardcoded LIFF_ID fallback
problem: src/middleware.ts uses hardcoded '2010006005-hye7KNGx' as LIFF_ID fallback because NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID build arg is not available in middleware at request time. If LIFF ID changes, the cookie bridge redirect will break silently.
solution: Removed hardcoded '2010006005-hye7KNGx' fallback. Now uses LIFF_ID runtime env var (primary) with NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID as fallback. Throws at startup if neither is set. Added LIFF_ID to docker-compose runtime env vars.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-28. Fix: inject LIFF_ID via Docker runtime env var or Next.js runtime config.

title: Consolidate display-name.ts (server) and getUserLabel (client)
problem: src/lib/display-name.ts has server-side alias resolution using prisma directly. FinanceContext has client-side getUserLabel doing the same thing via API. Two implementations of the same alias-first display logic. They could diverge.
notes: Found in retro 2026-05-28. Server-side uses resolveDisplayName/export async, client-side uses getUserLabel via state. Consider consolidating or documenting the split.

title: Production container is stale LIFF image — new login page not live
problem: After the LIFF→webapp pivot (commit 89b6e17), the running myfam-app container is still the pre-pivot LIFF image (env still has LIFF_ID, OLLAMA_BASE_URL points to host.docker.internal:11434). The user cannot log in on the deployed site until the image is rebuilt and the container restarted. Dev works; production does not.
solution: Fresh non-LIFF image built and deployed this session (myfam-app:latest, healthy, login page live at myfam.doctorboyz.com)
notes: Found in retro 2026-07-26. Fix: docker compose build myfam-app && docker compose up -d myfam-app. User said รอก่อน — waiting on go-ahead.

title: No password backfill strategy — DB reset leaves users passwordless
problem: The pivot switched auth to username/password (bcrypt). LIFF-era User rows had password IS NULL; fixed manually via SQL (UPDATE User SET password=<hash>). The seed sets passwords but was never re-run against this environment. There is no migration or backfill script, so a DB reset (or fresh deploy without re-seed) will leave users unable to log in again.
notes: Found in retro 2026-07-26. Fix: add a Prisma migration or seed script that backfills default password (4444) for users with password IS NULL, or document re-seed as required post-reset.

title: Font scale bump not visually verified — overflow risk
problem: Restored typography tokens from LIFF-compressed sizes (~10/12px → 14/16px, ~40% larger) and replaced ~40 hardcoded small font-sizes in component CSS with tokens via sed. Build passes but the rendered result was never visually verified. Risk: text overflow, truncation, or layout breakage on 480px mobile shell, especially in dashboard recent/budget cards and settings/family member cards.
notes: Found in retro 2026-07-26. Fix: run dev, screenshot /login /dashboard /transactions /settings/family at 480px; check for overflow/truncation.

title: Slip images stored as base64 in Postgres — move to object storage
problem: Transaction.slipImage stores multi-MB base64 strings in a Postgres column. The list endpoint had to strip them to avoid a 7.2MB payload; the per-tx endpoint still returns them. 28 slips = 6.8MB today, grows unbounded. Should move to S3/R2 with a URL reference.
notes: Found in retro 2026-07-29

title: No startup DB auth health check — env drift caught at first request
problem: entrypoint.sh runs prisma migrate deploy then next start. If the resolved DATABASE_URL password doesn't authenticate (e.g. shell env override drift), the app crash-loops on first migration with P1000 instead of failing fast with a clear message. Add a pre-flight auth check.
notes: Found in retro 2026-07-29

title: No persistent queue for Telegram updates — outages longer than retry window still lose slips
problem: Webhook acks 200 before processing; fetchWithRetry (2s/8s/30s) covers ~40s of transient failure. An outage longer than that loses the update permanently with no surfaced alert — user discovers it by noticing missing entries. Observed incidents (~1 min) were covered, but the residual risk is structural.
notes: Found in retro 2026-10-08 — accepted risk, revisit if longer outages appear

title: Bare keywords 'ยอด' and 'รายการ' don't match any bot command despite docs claiming they do
problem: docs/TELEGRAM_SETUP.md §5 says typing 'ยอด' or 'รายการ' works, but detectCommand (src/lib/bot/commands.ts:72,75) only matches ดูยอด/ยอดคงเหลือ/… and รายการล่าสุด/รายการวันนี้ — bare 'ยอด' and 'รายการ' fall through to AI extraction and the bot replies 'ไม่พบ: จำนวนเงิน'. Reproduced via sandbox POST 2026-10-08 as Lita. commands.test.ts never covered the bare keywords. Fix: add ยอด/รายการ to the regexes + tests (careful: 'ลบรายการล่าสุด' and 'แก้ยอด' must keep winning — bare 'ยอด' must not shadow edit_amount/reconcile flows, so anchor with word boundary or exact-match before fuzzy).
solution: Exact match in detectCommand (commit 5f98580); verified on production bot via sandbox
notes: Found while verifying Lita statement import via sandbox, retro 2026-10-08
